scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I live with my parents, and I pay them $200 a month, which they say is the market rate where we live. I've been living with them since I was pretty young, and most of the time, we get along. But recently, there was a bathroom flood, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of that, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. One day, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help them bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. Honestly, I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said that "in a minute" was now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. That led to a huge shouting match, and now they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their "golden child," and now they're throwing his success in my face. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, since I pay rent, that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole here? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, the dynamics of living with parents as an adult. There's an expectation of mutual respect and responsibility. I pay rent, which is a form of contributing to the household. But does that give me the right to refuse help with chores or errands? Then there's the incident itself. My parents asked for help, and I was playing a game. I told them I'd help in a minute, but they ended up making multiple trips. My dad got frustrated and took the controller, leading to an argument. Now they're threatening to leave and expecting me to find a place quickly. I also need to think about the emotional aspect. They brought up my brother, which seems like they're comparing me to him, which can be hurtful. That might have contributed to the argument. On the other hand, I feel like I'm contributing financially, and I expect some level of autonomy. But is refusing to help with groceries or chores a fair expectation? I also need to consider the practicality of finding a new place by Friday. That's a very short timeframe, and it might not be feasible. So, their demand might be unreasonable. But then, is my refusal to help a valid reason for them to want to leave? Or is there more to it? I also wonder about the underlying issues. The remodel due to the flooded bathroom might have caused more stress and tension between us. Maybe the argument was just the tip of the iceberg. So, putting it all together, am I the asshole for refusing to help with the groceries, or is there more to the situation that makes their reaction unreasonable? I think it's a bit of both. I should have been more considerate and helped them, especially since we're living in the same house. But their reaction seems extreme, especially the threat to leave and expecting me to find a place in such a short time. It might be a mix of both parties not handling the situation well. In the end, communication is key. Maybe we need to sit down and talk about our expectations and boundaries to avoid such conflicts in the future.
